newsitem.title: USA: Stop & Shop settles U.S. fraud claims.
newsitem.headline: Stop & Shop settles U.S. fraud claims.

text.p: Stop & Shop Cos. Inc. has agreed to pay $700,000 to settle civil claims stemming from allegedly fraudulent promotional practices by New England's biggest supermarket chain, U.S. Attorney Donald Stern said Friday.
In return, the federal prosecutor will drop all claims against Stop & Shop and its officers, directors and employees, the Quincy, Mass.-based company said in a statement.
The parties agreed to settle the claims to avoid further litigation, Stop & Shop said.

The government said its claims were based on the Mail Fraud Injunction Statute, and arose from promotional practices related to how Stop & Shop got reimbursed by food vendors for goods sold at "sale" prices.
Stop & Shop has discontinued the practices, the government statement said.

In one practice, called a "scan bill back," Stop & Shop did not disclose that the invoices it sent vendors inflated by 20 percent the amount of merchandise recorded by Stop & Shop's electronic scanners during a sale, the government said.
Stop & Shop did not disclose this 20 percent inflation factor to vendors, although the company contends its scan data was unreliable and grossly understated the actual amount of product sold.

In the second practice, called a "temporary price reduction," Stop & Shop did not disclose that the invoices it sent vendors were based on sales figures from all Stop & Shop stores, even though the sale prices had not been implemented in stores located in what Stop & Shop calls "Shaw's Zones."
The government said these are areas where Stop & Shop competes with Shaw's grocery stores.
Stop & Shop operates 185 supermarkets in Connecticut, Massachusetts, New York and Rhode Island.
